Key points
• The worldwide ingestion of added sugar/sucrose is still very high
• Sucrose is an important source of calories and promotes weight gain
• Energy independent negative effects of sucrose on metabolism are likely to exist
• Added sugars are suspected to dilute the intake of other nutrients
• The oral and intestinal microbiome interacts with added sugar
• Sugar/sucrose consumption by the ingestion of fruits is not harmful
• A reduction of the intake of added sugar is recommended
Introduction
While the diet of our ancestors was not completely free of sugar, the amount of simple carbohydrates ingested was low, reﬁned sugar
was not available and only few natural sources provided the disaccharide sucrose as such (e.g., fruits), and even fewer sources con-
tained some “free” sucrose as deﬁned by the WHO (e.g., honey). In contrast, modern western diets provide a large amount of the
